title: A memory whose text holds a lone underscore fails the doctor's search probe, so the doctor reports a healthy store corrupt
outcome: The doctor's full-text probe and memory search build queries from the same tokens the FTS5 tokenizer indexes, so a memory containing a lone underscore verifies, is found, and no longer makes the doctor (or migration import) call the store corrupt.
acceptance: A memory search whose query holds such a token still finds the memory by its other tokens; a test shows it.

A project memory whose title or body holds a token made only of underscores (such as a lone `_`) passes the doctor's object_fts probe; a test stores one and shows the doctor healthy, and fails without the fix.
Tokens that mix letters or digits with underscores keep today's search behaviour.
With the fixed build, doctor on the live Engram store no longer reports object_fts:d95ed1dc6b5f4b07b0cba67da05022b6:fts_index or object_fts:f5a0a9b7a5734e7c80f26df3b1061aa7:fts_index.

completion.summary:
The doctor no longer reports a healthy store corrupt when a memory holds a lone underscore. Landed as 2e836ae and installed as build a52ce998d0d8.
- fts_tokens drops fragments with no letter or digit. The unicode61 index treats `_` as a separator, so such a fragment could never match.
- fts_query returns None when nothing is left to search for, replacing the "__engram_no_match__" fallback that matched the phrase "engram no match". Memory search then finds nothing, and the doctor's probe is skipped while the stored-text check still runs.
- The change is query-side only, so no store needs projection repair.
- Tests: the tokenizer; a project memory with a lone underscore (doctor healthy, search, phrase order, the 16-token limit, index damage still reported); and a work-memory search with nothing searchable.
- Three review rounds, the last clean from both Codex and Claude. Full gate test-24a37374 passed.
- With the new build, the doctor is healthy on the Engram, PhoenixCodeNav and TermAl stores. On Engram it had reported the two false object_fts findings.
- Independent evaluation 511b3bc1 passed all four criteria.
- The remaining Unicode mismatches are tracked in w-1901af6c6f7e.
